title: Autopay Standing and Trade-In Chargebacks: Funding Desk Answers
content:
Autopay on the buyer's Kestrel financing sets the finance standing share of a title-delay chargeback under **Trade-In Agreements**.

**Which contract is read?** The contract under **Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts** on the purchase the trade is applied to: whether autopay is enrolled on it, and how many installments have been posted on it by autopay in the last twelve months.

**What are the shares?**

| Autopay on that contract | Installments posted by autopay in the last twelve months | Finance standing share |
|---|---|---|
| Enrolled | 2 or more | 0.85 |
| Enrolled | Fewer than 2 | 0.95 |
| Not enrolled, or no such contract | Any | One (no reduction) |

**How does it act?** The share multiplies the title-delay chargeback once; the chargeback is rounded to the nearest cent only once, at the end.

**Which payments count toward the 2?** Payment entries on that contract made through autopay, within the twelve months up to the day the chargeback is booked. Payments made online, by phone with an agent, by mail or by any other channel do not count.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** Autopay is enrolled and 1 installment has posted by autopay in the last twelve months: a chargeback of $5320.00 before this share becomes $5320.00 multiplied by 0.95, which is $5054.00. With 2 autopay installments it becomes $4522.00.
